Author: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery
Bench: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 76 
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 825 of 2023
Applicant :- Charan Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Rajiv Lochan Shukla,Sonal Bharti Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Bindeshwari Prasad Mishra,Chandra Prakash Tripathi Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
Heard Sri Rajiv Lochan Shukla, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Bindeshwari Prasad Mishra,
learned counsel for complainant and Sri Paritosh Malviya, learned A.G.A-I appearing for State.

Applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. after rejection of his Bail Application vide order dated 29.11.2022 in Case Crime No.151 of 2022 under Sections 323, 504, 506, 376(1) I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act,
2012, Police Station-Chaubia, District - Etawah.
In the present case, mother of a minor girl(victim) has lodged an FIR against present applicant that her daughter, aged about 15 years, was mentally disturbed.
On 18.05.2022 at 7.00 a.m. she went to shop of applicant who took advantage of mental status of victim, took her inside his house and raped her.

Victim told to her mother about incident, after that she came to lodge an F.I.R. earlier but police personnel have forced her to enter into a compromise, however, ultimately an F.I.R. was Charan Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125520659/
1 lodged on 21.09.2022 i.e. after about more than four months.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for applicant submits that on same set of allegation, informant has filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. on 21.07.2022 wherein a police report was submitted that parties have entered into compromise and learned court of Magistrate by an order dated 13.09.2022 rejected the application filed under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that said order was never challenged before any court.
Learned counsel further submits that at the time of lodging F.I.R., subsequently these facts were not brought on record before police personnel.

Learned counsel referred the statement of victim that alleged occurrence took place in a room which was locked from inside whereas the alleged eye-witnesses have stated that they have witnessed the applicant and girl lying on cot without their cloths.
Applicant is a 55 year old person and prosecution story is improbable.
Learned A.G.A. for State and learned counsel for complainant submit that there is no bar that after rejection of an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., F.I.R. cannot be lodged.

It was specifically alleged in F.I.R. that earlier too informant tried to lodge an F.I.R., however, she was forced to enter into a compromise and on the basis of said compromise, her application filed under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C. was rejected.

Learned counsel further submits that last seen witnesses stated that applicant and victim was lying without cloth and only ambiguity whether door was locked or not cannot make the entire prosecution story doubtful.
LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

(D) Over crowding of jail and gross delay in disposal of cases when undertrials are forced to remain in jail (not due to their fault) may give rise to possible situations that may justify invocation of Charan Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125520659/
2 Article 21 of Constitution, may also be considered along with other factors.

sentences.text: The statement of victim under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. are consistent that when victim went to shop of applicant, he took her inside the room and committed a wrong thing with her.
There are eye-witness account also that applicant and victim were lying on cot without cloths.

Counsel for applicant has placed major reliance on statement of victim that room was locked from inside, therefore, no one can see from outside, however, this can be considered by learned trial court on basis of evidence, which still to be led.
Even it is accepted that there is no eye-witness account, still statement of victim remains consistent that not only applicant took her inside the room but raped her also.

Applicant has taken advantage of trust of mother of victim who sent her to his shop to purchase grocery items, however, despite he is about to become senior citizen, took the girl(mentally disturbed) inside a room and committed offence of rape as well as taking note that till date statement of victim has not been recorded

,
therefore no case of bail is made out and learned trial court is directed to record the statement of victim preferably within a period of three months from today.
Thereafter applicant will have liberty to file a fresh bail application.
Accordingly, bail application is rejected.
